question: Why does head-derived covariance reallocation lose on separate-head sources despite strong function association on shared sources: branch prediction quality, residual branch mass or a changed R prior?
analysis: Retain the frozen 16^3 primary macro priors and rho=32 branch evidence/densities. Decompose A17 minus same-pool I/R into the F/G contribution at fixed A17 q and the q-calibration contribution. Report pure F and G forecast contrasts with I and their previously accumulated log-evidence ratios. Compute I/F/G/R posterior masses before steps 9 and 24, plus the change over the path. Average eight held tasks within each archive, then pair 16 seeds separately in both source groups and both prior arms.
scope: Diagnostic accounting only. Pure branch scores and removed-branch contrasts do not define new winning methods. No source-fit covariance estimate is treated as an independent prediction label, and no target data or full-archive eta information is used to condition held-task weights.
within_fg_breakdown: Before inspecting attribution results, also define each head's exact accounting contribution as the average of its two removal-order log-score differences, transferring removed mass to I. These two contributions sum to the combined F/G effect; they are explanatory quantities, not fitted weights or additional methods.
decision: Judge whether meaningful conditional function information is being erased by a common macro prior or whether the proposed equal-within-selection reallocation itself predicts poorly. Identify the required form of a future source-trained joint prior and any missing fold-aware source information; do not retune or revive A17 using these results.
limitations: Explanatory reuse of A17 source development evidence, not independent confirmation or a basis for choosing the best seed/group-specific weight. Source associations alone do not establish decision benefits.
